metadata.title: Garmin Personal API MCP — Local, Read-only Garmin MCP Server
metadata.description: A local, read-only, open-source Garmin MCP server for activities, sleep, HRV, Body Battery, heart rate, and wellness data through the official Garmin Personal API.

hero.description: Use the official Garmin Personal API to bring your activities, sleep, HRV, Body Battery, heart rate, and wellness data into a compatible AI client. The open-source server runs entirely on your computer and never asks for your Garmin password.

scenarios.question: How was my recovery yesterday?
scenarios.answer: You slept 7 h 42 m, overnight HRV was inside your recent baseline, and Body Battery rose by 61 points. Yesterday looks recovered enough for a normal training day, but this is not a medical or readiness diagnosis.

scenarios.question: Show me what changed in my latest long run.
calls: Inspect laps, heart rate, and power
scenarios.answer: The run was 18.4 km. Your final 5 km was 11 sec/km faster while average heart rate rose 6 bpm. Power stayed comparatively stable, so the faster finish did not come with a matching power spike.

scenarios.question: Did sleep and stress change this week?
scenarios.answer: Average sleep was 24 minutes shorter than the previous week and high-stress time increased on three workdays. Body Battery also started those mornings lower. That is a useful pattern to review, not proof of a medical cause.

how.title: Garmin Personal API data, fetched locally when you ask.
how.description: When you ask a question, the local server fetches the required data from the Garmin Personal API and returns the result to your AI client. This project runs no cloud relay and stores no Garmin data remotely; any further processing depends on the AI provider and privacy policy you choose.

flow.title: Your local MCP host
flow.description: A compatible AI client chooses a Garmin tool for the question you asked. No browser extension or hosted connector is required.

flow.title: The local MCP server
flow.description: The Node.js process validates inputs, controls date ranges and sample volume, then returns structured results to your AI client.

flow.title: Garmin Personal API
flow.description: Your token is sent over HTTPS directly to the Garmin Personal API. The server exposes read operations only.

how.authTitle: Your Garmin Personal API key completes authorization on your computer—not in chat.
how.authDescription: Create a Garmin Personal API key in Garmin Connect and authorize once. The CLI stores the key and cached bearer token in a local file readable only by you. It never uses the username-and-password scraping flow found in older Garmin Connect integrations.

data.title: One local interface for activity, recovery, and health questions.
data.description: The server maps Garmin Personal API endpoints to twenty-five deliberate MCP tools—not one oversized endpoint and not a generic scraper.

topics.title: Garmin activity API and FIT recordings
topics.body: Search activities by date, sport, or title; inspect the activity summary and workout steps; then decode a Garmin FIT file only when lap or sampled recording detail is needed. Power, pace, cadence, heart rate, temperature, and GPS coordinates stay tied to their original units.

topics.title: Garmin sleep, HRV, and Body Battery data
topics.body: Read a single day or compare summaries across a bounded range. Sleep stages, overnight HRV, Body Battery charge and drain, and stress can be placed in the same answer without pretending that a wellness signal is a medical diagnosis.

topics.title: Heart rate and daily health summaries
topics.body: Query daily summaries, steps, hydration, continuous heart-rate aggregates, SpO2, weight, food logs, and wellness activities. Exact high-frequency samples are omitted by default so a simple Garmin health question does not flood the model context.

topics.title: Profile, heart-rate zones, and fitness context
topics.body: Use the Garmin profile, configured heart-rate zones, fitness age, and cycle data to interpret a number in the context of the person it belongs to. Every tool remains a data retrieval tool; it does not issue a diagnosis or edit a Garmin account.

privacy.title: A local Garmin MCP with a boundary you can inspect.
privacy.description: This project does not host or forward your Garmin data. Tool results do enter the AI client and model you choose, where that provider's privacy policy applies.
boundaries: Your Garmin Personal API key and cached bearer token are stored only on your computer.
Every exposed Garmin operation is a GET. There are no workout, device, or account writes.
High-frequency samples and exact FIT coordinates are omitted unless explicitly requested.
The server has no analytics, crash reporting, account system, database, or remote relay.

items.question: What is Garmin Personal API MCP?
items.answer: It is an open-source Node.js MCP server that exposes your own Garmin data as twenty-five read-only tools. A compatible AI client launches it directly on your computer; this project does not run a hosted Garmin connector.

items.question: Where do I create a Garmin Personal API key?
items.answer: Create the key on Garmin Connect's dedicated Personal API Token settings page and copy it immediately because Garmin shows it only once. Then run the local auth command. The CLI exchanges the key for a bearer token and stores both only in a user-only file on your computer.

items.question: Does this use the official Garmin Personal API?
items.answer: Yes. The server uses the official Garmin Personal API for data requests and Garmin’s official FIT SDK for activity recordings. It does not use a username-and-password Garmin Connect scraper.

items.question: Can it change my Garmin account or push workouts to a device?
items.answer: No. v0.1 exposes read-only operations backed by Garmin Personal API GET endpoints. It cannot create workouts, update profile data, change settings, or push content to a Garmin device.

items.question: Can I use this Garmin MCP with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, or VS Code?
items.answer: Yes, when the installed client can launch a local MCP server. This page has copy-and-paste setup requests for Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor. Claude Desktop, VS Code, and other clients that support local MCP servers can use the generic npx configuration in the advanced setup section.

items.question: Can my AI client install and configure Garmin Personal API MCP for me?
items.answer: Yes. Paste the tailored setup request into Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor. Its agent can check the local runtime, run the package, register the local MCP server, and verify the connection. The auth command opens a temporary 127.0.0.1 page where you enter the Garmin API key yourself; the key never belongs in chat.

items.question: Does my Garmin data stay entirely on my computer?
items.answer: The API key, token cache, and server stay local, and this project runs no relay. Tool results are returned to the MCP host you selected and may be processed by its model under that provider’s privacy policy.

items.question: Can an AI inspect Garmin FIT activity data?
items.answer: Yes. The activity recording tool can decode laps, sessions, and sampled FIT records such as heart rate, power, cadence, pace, temperature, and coordinates. High-frequency samples and exact GPS coordinates require explicit options.

items.question: Which operating systems and Node.js versions are supported?
items.answer: Node.js 22 or newer is required on macOS, Windows, or Linux. Windows hosts that cannot execute npx directly can launch it through cmd /c, as shown in the configuration tabs.

items.question: Why did the local Garmin MCP server fail to start?
items.answer: Run npx -y @trainingloadai/garmin-personal-api-mcp doctor. It checks Node.js, the credential source, local file permissions, Garmin token exchange, and a read-only profile request without starting a remote service.
